The retiree's own text declared it a classification error (Wolof is Atlantic, not Bantu) kept only to document the anomaly. The keeper has 106 inbound files; the retiree's sources and sub-groups are folded in, its self-description is not.

A digit suffix is not an identifier. The fiche describes the Bena-Lulua, the western dialect group of the Luba-Kasai, and takes their ethnonym; the exonym that named the database designation is removed.
The fiche covers the Manala royal house of the Southern Ndebele; the digit suffix is replaced by the sub-group's name. PPL_NDEBELE_SA remains the umbrella fiche.
The fiche covers the Ndzundza house; renamed alongside its pair so that neither sub-group carries the bare Southern Ndebele label that the umbrella PPL_NDEBELE_SA already covers.

Not a duplicate of PPL_NSENGA. The Senga are a Tumbuka sub-group (ISO tum, ZMB/MWI, 213 000); the Nsenga an independent people with their own language (ISO nse, ZMB/MOZ/ZWE, 1 179 000). Both fiches say so, and Ethnologue agrees.
Not a duplicate of PPL_KISII. The Kisi of Tanzania (ISO kiz, 21 000) and the Abagusii of Kenya (ISO guz, 3 100 000) are unrelated peoples; the near-identical ids are a coincidence of transcription.

Not a duplicate of PPL_RWANDAIS_TUTSI or PPL_RWANDAIS_HUTU. Banyarwanda is the ethnolinguistic whole; Hutu and Tutsi are social categories within it. Twelve patronym dossiers point at the umbrella because a Rwandan name is neither Hutu nor Tutsi.

Not a duplicate of PPL_TONGA_ZAMBIA. Toka and Leya are named sub-groups with their own territory around Mosi-oa-Tunya and their own ethnonym; the corpus keeps sub-group fiches beside the whole, as it does for the Ndebele houses.
